newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN human rights chief to visit Rwanda, Burundi.
newsitem.headline: UN human rights chief to visit Rwanda, Burundi.

text.p: U.N. human rights chief Jose Ayala Lasso will go to Rwanda and Burundi next week to assess security in the region following the killing of five of his staff last week by Rwandan gunmen, a spokesman said on Friday.

Ayalo Lasso, criticised by some diplomats and human rights groups for his relatively low profile in drawing public attention to abuses and violence, will spend a day and a half each in the capitals of Rwanda and Burundi, Kigali and Bujumbura.

He will meet government officials in Kigali and seek the result of a state investigation into the killings of four U.N. human rights monitors -- a Briton, a Cambodian and two Rwandans -- in an ambush last Tuesday in Cyangugu in southwestern Rwanda. Their Rwandan driver later died of his wounds.
The U.N. human rights office has largely suspended its work in the tiny central African country after the killings, the U.N. spokesman said.
His staff have criticised Ayala Lasso for not going to Rwanda immediately after the killings, which have underlined the vulnerability of relief staff in conflict zones.
